children: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) shares fell nearly 4% on Wednesday, pushing its market capitalization below Microsoft’s (MSFT) and dropping the AI chipmaker to third place among the world's most valuable companies, as investors assess risks ahead of CEO Jensen Huang’s congressional testimony next week.

At market close, Nvidia’s market capitalization stood at $3.61 trillion, below Microsoft’s $3.64 trillion and Apple’s (AAPL) $5.17 trillion. Nvidia's valuation has fallen from a peak of $5.77 trillion in early October.

children: “NVDA shares traded 30% higher on the news of Jensen’s return, then quickly gave back 13% in the two following trading days, underscoring that the Nvidia investment case still has five unknowns,” Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster wrote in a blog post.

These include how “Jensen 2.0” will lead the chipmaker, the impact of China restrictions on next year’s revenue, the impact of the “blue wave” on data center buildout, the pace of customer financing, and “Jensen’s trip next week to Capitol Hill.”

“In the end, I believe these five concerns are outweighed by the company’s silicon and software leadership,” Munster said, adding that despite risks, he believes Nvidia will grow faster than Wall Street’s estimates over the next three years.
In a dramatic about-turn, the Nvidia board reinstated Huang as CEO on Monday, days after saying they had decided against it. The move came after President Donald Trump
for his return.
Nvidia Fundamentals Unchanged, Says Investor
Nvidia’s fundamental picture hasn’t changed, investor Gary Black said in an X post, adding that the stock's fundamentals are now even more impressive than before.

“$NVDA now trading at a forward P/E of 8.9x and an EV/EBITDA of 7.3x - their lowest levels in at least 10 years. This compares to forward long-term rev growth of 25% and forward long-term EPS growth rate of 28% - PEGs that are unmatched among mega cap stocks,” Black wrote.

“Fundamentally for NVDA, nothing much has changed - there has been no earnings or revenue degradation in recent weeks. If anything, fundamentals are now likely better since the Trump administration has essentially signaled there will be no clamp down on export controls on NVDA’s chip sales through Asia.”
Nvidia Saga: Other Updates

In a development widely shared across social media, restaurant chain Denny’s reinstated a plaque at its Berryessa Drive location marking the 1993 booth where Huang and co-founders Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem brainstormed setting up Nvidia.
The plaque, first installed in 2023, was removed earlier this month after news of Huang’s alleged affairs emerged, but Denny’s restored it after contacting Nvidia.

In other news, Pentagon officials were working on a plan to use the Defense Production Act to nudge Nvidia to reinstall Jensen Huang as CEO, with the argument that it related to national security, Washington Post reported, citing its sources.
Retail View For NVDA
On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for NVDA dipped over the past week but remained ‘bullish.’
“$NVDA If the upcoming hearings determine that Jensen did anything treasonous, this stock might not stay above a hundred. 1.5 trading days till first hearing,”
a trader.
Another trader wrote: “$NVDA bears are gonna get short squeezed hard on friday.”
Year-to-date, NVDA stock is down nearly 20%.
At the market close, Nvidia’s market cap slid to $3.61 trillion, below Microsoft’s $3.64 trillion.
Nvidia’s fundamental picture hasn’t changed, investor Gary Black said.
Retail sentiment for NVDA dipped over the past week but remained ‘bullish’ as analysts prepare for CEO Jensen Huang’s congressional hearing next week.

title: Nvidia’s Market Cap Falls Below Microsoft’s: Analyst Flags Five Overhangs For NVDA Stock
